content.text: This one is going to be annoying to fix.  Does anyone have some preferences about how to indicate where the relevant Spring configuration is for the rebuilders? We may be able to just load all the beans from the web subdirectory...
+1 to extra-loading from spring/web. Why make more config unless it turns out we have to?
Only because I'm not sure I can load all the beans without the servlet APIs loaded from the container.  But I'll give it a try.

Urg. It sounds like we can't stand up a rebuilder framework without (essentially) a Fedora server. But we want to be minimal. Maybe a longer-term maintenance mode for the rebuilder should include breaking it apart and rewiring with Spring-- no more RebuildServer.java, if that makes sense?
It makes lots of sense: None of the Server impls are good for that much anymore.  But that's too ambitious for 3.6.2.
Agreed. Current fix plan sounds good. Let's revisit the general issue of the rebuilder design for 3.7.

So, loading the web beans is not so great (the rebuild server needs to load the RI for the web beans, but appears to need to exclude it for the RI rebuilder).  I'm falling back on the env property with a default value hack, which is really quite ugly.

The PolicyIndexRebuilder does not have access to the PolicyIndex it needs, because the RebuildServer does not load the requisite Spring beans. This leads to a NullPointerException.  It can be worked around by copying the PolicyIndex configuration, and configuring an additional bean for the rebuilder like so:

renderedFields.description:
The PolicyIndexRebuilder does not have access to the PolicyIndex it needs, because the RebuildServer does not load the requisite Spring beans. This leads to a NullPointerException. It can be worked around by copying the PolicyIndex configuration, and configuring an additional bean for the rebuilder like so:

<bean id="org.fcrepo.server.security.xacml.pdp.data.PolicyIndexRebuilder2"
class="org.fcrepo.server.security.xacml.pdp.data.PolicyIndexRebuilder" >
<property name="policyIndex"
ref="org.fcrepo.server.security.xacml.pdp.data.PolicyIndex" />
</bean>
